title: Ex Machina : Annihilation Requires Intellectual Sacrifice

commenti.body: I like your comparison a lot, but I think you're giving both Caleb and Sgt Howie a bit of an easy ride here. They don't deserve death, but they're not in any way "morally upstanding" - they may think they are, but that's not the same thing. Howie is an intolerant, closed-minded prude, and Caleb is the face of the superficially benign mask the patriarchy ways to legitimise the subjugation of women. Lord Summerisle and Nathan are antagonists who a harm to society in more obviously violent ways, whereas Howie and Caleb represent individuals who passively contribute to systemic injustices through their worldviews (particularly Howie).

Good call. I admit "morally upstanding" is a generalisation of superficial presentation. I wouldn't necessarily call Sargent Howie a prude because he has a palpable fear of intimacy and God when he is presented with temptation in Willow.
